messages:
michelle: Quick sync — I'm drafting the PRD section called "Security acceptance scenarios" for audit logs / KMS / HSM needs. Need to capture all acceptance criteria + edge cases before we freeze scope for the 1.0 launch. Putting questions and proposals below.

raj: Can we get a concrete list of customer asks? I know one enterprise asked for 7-year audit retention, BYOK with HSM-backed keys, and ability to stream audit logs to their SIEM. Any others?

sylvia: For SOC2 vs ISO there are different evidence artifacts. SOC2 wants demonstrable controls (config, logs, key access lists), ISO wants documented procedures + signed attestations. We should enumerate both.

nathan: Proposal (starter): default audit retention = 365 days, enterprise tier supports long retention (configurable to 7 years archived). Default key model = platform-managed KMS; enterprise option = BYOK with HSM + key attestation. :thumbsup: 

eva: Legal note: long retention increases PII risk and DSAR complexity. If customers ask for 7yrs we need documented deletion/subject-request playbook that shows how we handle partial deletion while preserving tamper-evident audit trail.

raj: Technical edgecases to capture: key rotation (how to rotate customer BYOK without breaking old audit encryption), key compromise (re-encrypt history?), partial log corruption during rolling upgrades, and export integrity checks. Minimal config snippet to illustrate what we mean:

```
audit:
  retention_days: 365
  archive_policy: "cold-archive"
  export_enabled: true
  export_destination: "s3://<org>-audit"
  kms_model: "platform|byok-hsm"
```

michelle: @sylvia @eva can you list the acceptance testable scenarios we need in the PRD? Think: 1) log immutability, 2) tamper detection, 3) export + validation, 4) key rotation without data loss, 5) DSAR-compatible redaction flow.

sylvia: Acceptance examples (short):
- Immutability: attempt to mutate stored audit record -> system rejects and generates tamper event.
- Tamper detect: HMAC chain validation fails -> alert + quarantine.
- Export: exported archive includes signed manifest + checksum.
- Key rotation: re-encrypt archive with new key and verify manifests.
- Compromise scenario: revoke compromised key and rotate; provide signed attestation of re-encryption.

nathan: Launch gates (suggested): Security review complete, Legal sign-off for retention policy, QA runs canary with a customer on BYOK, Ops run dry-run export. If any gate fails, rollback to platform-managed KMS for that customer.

raj: Performance note: indexing audit log full-text for 7 years will be expensive. Consider two-tier retention: searchable (hot) 90d, archived (cold) 7y with no full-text index and object-level checksums. This needs explicit acceptance criteria in PRD because it changes UX.

eva: Compliance ask: include a signed log sampling protocol for auditors: "how we sample exports, how we sign manifests, and how we map events to controls". Also document SLA for evidence delivery (e.g., 10 business days).

michelle: Edge-case: GDPR erase request — can we pseudonymize instead of fully deleting audit entries? We need a defensible approach auditors accept: mark PII as redacted but keep record id + HMAC chain intact so immutability still holds.

sylvia: Agreed. Add test: run DSAR -> exported evidence must show redaction markers + verify that verification chain still passes. If not, fail.

ops-bot: link: https://redwood-internal/docs/prd/security-acceptance-scenarios (draft) :eyes: 

raj: One more edge: partial writes during outage -> duplicate entries after retry. Acceptance: dedupe by request id within 24h window and surface duplicates in audit UI for manual reconciliation.

nathan: Ownership matrix we need in PRD: Security owns threat scenarios, Eng owns implementation + tests, Product owns gate decisions, Legal owns retention terms. Add timeline: PRD freeze in 2 weeks, security review in week 3, canary week 4.

eva: I'll draft the legal blurb for retention exceptions and evidence SLA. I'll need a quick checklist of what data is included in export (headers, payload, metadata) — @raj can you paste the export schema?

raj: Will paste schema into the PRD doc later. For now: exports include event_ts, org_id, user_id (pseudonymized if requested), action, target, raw_payload (redacted), signature_manifest.

michelle: Great — next actions: (1) @sylvia list test cases + acceptance criteria in doc, (2) @raj add export schema + index cost estimate, (3) @eva legal retention text + SLA, (4) @nathan update launch gates and timeline. I'll consolidate and ping for sign-offs. :thumbsup: 

sylvia: I'll add the threat matrix and HSM key compromise recovery steps. Also propose we require HSM attestation docs from vendors for BYOK HSM mode.

nathan: Quick decision: default to 365d hot + 7y cold-archive for enterprise with opt-in pricing. If no objections by EOD Friday, I'll put that into the PRD scope. :clock1: 

michelle: No objections so far. Locking into draft scope pending the items above. Last_message: thanks everyone — please add comments in the PRD doc. :raised_hands:
